caseno: Appeal from Original Decree (FA) No. 122 of 1992
lawyer:
Mainul Islam, Advocate ----- For the Appellant. 
ASM Wahidul Momin Chowdhury, Advocate ----- For Respondent No.1.
parties:
Siraj Mia (Md) ----- Appellant 
Vs 
Nasima Akhter and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Tafazzul Islam J: This. Appeal, at the instance of the plaintiff appellant is directed against the judgment and decree dated 24-3-92 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Additional Court, Narayanganj, in Title Suit No. 40 of 1991 dismissing the suit. 

 3. The aforesaid suit was filed on 9-2-89 and on 15-2-89 the plaintiff also filed an application praying for an order of temporary injunction restraining the defendant No.1 from transferring the suit land to others or dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land or disturb the peaceful possession of the plaintiff in the suit land and then show Cause notice having been issued the defendant No.1 duly appeared in the said suit and on 23-2-89 she prayed for time for filing written objection but ultimately, she neither filed written objection nor any written statement and she also did not contest the suit and then on 24-3-92 the suit was taken up for ex parte hearing and during hearing the plaintiff examined himself as PW I and also the service PW 2 and PW 2 proved the baina dated 4-3-88 as Exhibit 1 and his signature as well as the signature of defendant No.1 in the said baina as Exhibits 1/1 and 1/2 and after hearing, the learned Subordinate Judge, by the impugned judgment and decree. Dismissed the suit holding that no attesting witnesses of the baina came forward to prove Exhibit 1, the baina, and that the plaintiff also did not produce and prove the Deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz dated 15-12-85 by which the defendant No.1 got the suit land from her father. 

 5. Mr ASM Wahidul Momen Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the defendant No.1 respondent, submits that although the grounds shown for dismissal of the suit is not satisfactory but the facts remain that the plaintiff, even in the case of ex parte disposal, is required to prove his own case and, in the eye of law, the plaintiff was required to prove the tender and/or payment of the balance amount of Taka 1,63,000 and that PW 1, being the plaintiff, is an interested witness and so the plaintiff was required to examine another independent witness to prove that the plaintiff tendered money to the defendant No.1 and further, though in the plaint it was categorically stated that the plaintiff, out of Taka 1,63,000 paid Taka 5000 at the time of execution of the baina and then even after tender, the balance consideration money was not accepted but PW 1, in his deposition, completely made out a new case to the effect that he paid the balance consideration of Taka 1,63,000 but in spite of that the defendant No.1 did not execute and register the sale deed. Mr Chowdhury next submits that the appellant in his application filed under Order XLI rule 27 CPC has stated that for her operation she needed money urgently and so she agreed to sell the suit land to the plaintiff but the plaintiff merely paid Taka 5000 at the time of the execution of the baina and did not pay the balance amount of Taka 1,63,000 within two months as stipulated in the baina and that in the present case, time was very much the essence of the contract and so due to non payment of balance consideration amount within two months, the very purpose of executing the baina got frustrated and the plaintiff, by keeping with himself the balance amount of Taka 1,63,000 for more than 14 years, got advantage, out of the said amount whereas the defendant No. 1 faced the hardship and moreover, it is only due to the part of the Advocate that the suit was decreed ex parte and so she should not suffer for such laches on the part of her learned Advocate and further, the prayer for specific performance of contract is also liable to be rejected on the ground of hardship because if decree for specific performance of contract is passed the defendant will suffer irreparable loss and injury. 

 16. Accordingly, in view of the fact that baina has been proved and in case of agreement for sale of immovable property time is not the essence of contract and during three years at the trial stage defendant did not care to enquire about the fate of the suit, we are of the view that ends of justice will be met if decree for specific performance is passed subject to payment to the respondent solatium of Taka 2,37,000 over and above Taka 1,63,000. 

 17. In the result the appeal is allowed and order as to cost and the judgment and decree dated 24-3-92 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Additional Court, Narayanganj in Title Suit No. 40 of 1991 is set aside and decree for specific performance as prayed for by the plaintiff/appellant is passed subject to the condition that the appellant will pay to the respondent solatium of Taka 2,37,000 over and above balance consideration money of Taka 1,63,000 and this amount of Taka 4,00,000 is to be paid by the appellant to the respondent within three months from the date of signing of this judgment and decree and, in default, interest @ 20% will accrue on the amount which remains unpaid after two months.
